questions.question: What is the most common indication for performing a "Screening" Breast MRI?
choices: High-risk screening (e.g., BRCA mutation or >20% lifetime risk)
questions.detail: MRI is used as a supplemental tool specifically for women with significantly elevated genetic or calculated lifetime risk.

questions.question: On a Breast MRI, a "Type III" (Washout) enhancement kinetic curve is:
choices: Only seen in the male breast
questions.detail: Malignant tumors often exhibit rapid uptake followed by rapid washout of contrast because of leaky, disorganized neovascularity.

questions.question: A "Type I" (Persistent) enhancement curve is most commonly associated with:
choices: Benign lesions (e.g., fibroadenomas or lymph nodes)
questions.detail: Type I curves demonstrate progressive enhancement over time, which is generally considered a benign feature.

questions.question: "Non-Mass Enhancement" (NME) on MRI refers to enhancement that is:
choices: Not a mass and follows a specific distribution (e.g., linear or segmental)
questions.detail: NME is an area of enhancement lacking space-occupying features and is frequently seen in cases of DCIS.

questions.question: Which NME distribution pattern is considered the MOST suspicious for DCIS?
questions.detail: Segmental or linear enhancement is highly suspicious as it follows the path of a ductal system toward the nipple.

questions.question: Breast MRI is typically performed during which days of the menstrual cycle to minimize background parenchymal enhancement (BPE)?
questions.detail: Background enhancement is at its lowest during the second week of the cycle when estrogen levels are rising but haven't peaked.

questions.question: Which MRI sequence is used to suppress the signal from normal breast fat to highlight enhancing lesions?
questions.detail: Contrast-enhanced sequences require fat suppression to distinguish between bright contrast enhancement and bright fat signal.

questions.question: "Background Parenchymal Enhancement" (BPE) on MRI is categorized as:
questions.detail: It is essential to report the degree of BPE because significant enhancement can mask underlying small cancers.

questions.question: MRI has a very high sensitivity for detecting which type of breast cancer, which can be occult on mammography?
questions.detail: While ILC often fails to form a discrete mass or calcifications, its infiltrative enhancement is frequently visible on MRI.

questions.question: A "rim-enhancing" mass with central high T2 signal (water-like) is characteristic of:
questions.detail: Both inflammatory collections (abscesses) and post-traumatic fluid collections (fat necrosis) can present with rim enhancement.

questions.question: Which MRI finding is a "classic" benign indicator for a mass?
questions.detail: Non-enhancing internal septations are a characteristic feature often observed in benign fibroadenomas.

questions.question: "DWI" (Diffusion Weighted Imaging) in breast MRI is used as a supplemental tool where a LOW "ADC" value suggests:
choices: A malignant lesion (due to high cellularity)
questions.detail: Restricted diffusion, indicated by a low ADC value, is a hallmark of dense and hypercellular malignant tissue.

questions.question: MRI is the "gold standard" for evaluating the integrity of which type of implant?
questions.detail: The primary role of MRI in implant imaging is the identification of "silent" intracapsular silicone ruptures.

questions.question: "Focus" on breast MRI is defined as a tiny area of enhancement measuring:
questions.detail: A focus is a dot of enhancement too small to be further characterized by its morphology.

questions.question: What is the recommended BI-RADS assessment for a suspicious MRI finding that has no correlate on mammography or ultrasound?
questions.detail: Suspicious findings identified only on MRI require biopsy, often performed under MRI guidance.
